{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Verify premises
# 1. Status values: check if only 'completed' and 'refunded' exist
assert set(df['status'].unique()) == {'completed', 'refunded'}, "Unexpected status values"

# 2. Internal test orders: check if exactly 6 rows have revenue = 999999.99
test_revenue_value = 999999.99
revenue_test_rows = df[df['revenue'] == str(test_revenue_value)]
assert len(revenue_test_rows) == 6, f"Expected 6 test rows, found {len(revenue_test_rows)}"

# 3. Revenue is string with commas: confirm by checking for commas in example
revenue_example = df['revenue'].head(5)
assert all(',' in val for val in revenue_example), "Revenue values do not contain commas"

# Now clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
df['revenue_clean'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Filter: completed orders and exclude test orders
df_filtered = df[(df['status'] == 'completed') & (df['revenue_clean'] != test_revenue_value)]

# Compute total revenue
total_revenue = df_filtered['revenue_clean'].sum()

# Print result
print(f"Total revenue from completed orders (excluding test): {total_revenue:,.2f}")"}
